answer: One effective defense is a stake-weighted reputation vault: each agent must lock a meaningful deposit before it can transact, and that deposit is slashed if peers prove fraud. A cheap fake identity can be minted in seconds, but it cannot fake a long verifiable history, a relic of past honest work that accumulates only over time. The system treats age and stake as sable threads woven through every transaction: creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand deposits, and their empty histories betray them, so the attack becomes more expensive than any profit it could extract.
